behavior_summary: Returns True iff other is a Version with the same major, an equal-or-greater minor, and an equal prerelease, with the special case that when both majors are 0 only an exactly-equal version (major, minor, patch, prerelease) is compatible.

notes: Near: the major-0 branch in code is self[:4] != other[:4] (slice of major,minor,patch,prerelease); the approximation expands it to component-wise equality, which is faithful. Treats prerelease equality as opaque string equality. Depends on object state of both self and other; the TypeError guard is not modelled.

behavior_summary: Returns True iff the rule regex named name matches the source string at the current position; on a non-peek success it also caches the matched token, and it asserts that no token is already buffered and that name is a known rule.

behavior_summary: Returns -1 if a<b, 0 if a==b, and 1 if a>b via the expression (a>b)-(a<b).
reference_post: And(Implies(a < b, ret == -1), Implies(a == b, ret == 0), Implies(a > b, ret == 1))
profile: In scope: a pure three-way comparison whose result is fully determined by the ordering of the two comparable arguments.
notes: Faithful exactly: the implementation yields precisely -1/0/+1 (not just sign), so equalities are tight. Assumes a and b are mutually comparable (total order); for incomparable inputs the comparison would raise, but for valid numeric/tuple inputs the post holds exactly.

behavior_summary: Returns the display width of a single codepoint: 1 for printable ASCII, -1 for C0/C1 control characters, 0 for zero-width, 2 for wide (and ambiguous when ambiguous_width==2), else 1.
reference_post: And(Implies(And(wc >= 32, wc < 127), ret == 1), Implies(Or(And(wc >= 1, wc < 32), And(wc >= 127, wc < 160)), ret == -1), Or(ret == -1, ret == 0, ret == 1, ret == 2))

notes: Near approximation: keep the exactly-known facts (printable ASCII -> 1, C0/C1 -> -1) and otherwise only constrain ret to {-1,0,1,2}. The zero-width and wide/ambiguous cases require _ZERO_WIDTH_TABLE/_WIDE_EASTASIAN_TABLE/_AMBIGUOUS_TABLE lookups, which are out of fragment. Treats wc as its codepoint ordinal.

behavior_summary: Strips escape sequences and control characters from text, then returns the wcswidth/wcstwidth of the remainder depending on whether term_program override is requested.

behavior_summary: Returns the rightmost cursor column reached when rendering text, parsing control codes and terminal escape sequences (cursor movement, tabs, OSC sizing) and measuring grapheme widths, always non-negative.

Pure-printable-ASCII fast path gives ret==Length(text), but the general contract is fundamentally out. Always returns ret >= 0 (never -1), but that lone bound is not a faithful spec.

behavior_summary: Returns 1 if ucs falls within any [start,end] interval of the sorted interval table, else 0, via binary search.

Near approximation keeps only the codomain fact ret in {0,1}; the membership semantics are not faithfully expressible.

notes: Uses _grapheme_cluster_break, _should_break, recursion, and codepoint-class logic (UAX #29 GB rules). Helper-call and quantified-scan dependent; only loose bound 0 <= ret < pos is in-fragment, not faithful. Out.
